title: Object Storage Access from S3 PUT from unexpected APAC region

compliance.assurance_rationale: Saved search evidence for AU-2 when alert outputs are archived.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:s3:accesslogs` events with `operation=REST.PUT.OBJECT` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.14.13 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:s3:accesslogs` traffic without `operation=REST.PUT.OBJECT`. Confirm UC-4.14.13 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:s3:accesslogs` collected via Splunk Add-on for AWS; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: UC-4.14.13 — Object Storage Access from S3 PUT from unexpected APAC region: queries AWS `aws:s3:accesslogs` for scenario 'Object Storage Access from S3 PUT from unexpected APAC region' (operation=REST.PUT.OBJECT...) and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: Cross-border PUT operations from high-risk regions may indicate compromised credentials. UC-4.14.13 operationalizes this as a high-priority security alert on AWS audit and edge telemetry.
implementation: Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=aws sourcetype=aws:s3:accesslogs.
visualization: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report.
knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for AWS with the modular input for `aws:s3:accesslogs`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.14.1.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `bucket` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=aws sourcetype=aws:s3:accesslogs.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:s3:accesslogs" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:s3:accesslogs" operation=REST.PUT.OBJECT | lookup geoip clientIP AS country | search country IN ("CN","RU")
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.14.13_object_storage_access_fr_13"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:s3:accesslogs` in `index=aws` to detect object storage access from s3 put from unexpected apac region. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon S3 console Server access logging for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `bucket` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_14_13_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for AWS and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of object storage access from s3 put from unexpected apac region so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
